summary: AI observability has become essential as LLM deployments scale, with the market growing to an estimated $2.69 billion in 2026 and projected to reach $9.26 billion by 2030 at a 36.2% CAGR. Gartner predicts that by 2028 LLM observability investments will account for 50% of GenAI deployments, up from 15% in early 2026. These tools help teams trace prompts, track token costs, evaluate output quality, and connect AI issues to broader application performance problems.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: LLM traces, spans, prompt/response chains, agent runs, and evaluation metrics across LangChain and non-LangChain applications.
features: Per-trace tracing and debugging of chains and agents
tools.pricing: Developer tier free at 5,000 traces/month; Plus at $39 per seat/month; overage around $2.50 per thousand traces at standard retention; custom Enterprise pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams building on the LangChain/LangGraph ecosystem that need deep trace-level debugging and integrated evaluations.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: LLM API requests through a gateway/proxy, including cost, latency, token usage, and caching metrics.
tools.pricing: Free Hobby tier (10K requests/month); Pro at $79/month (unlimited seats, usage-based beyond included volume); Team at $799/month (adds SOC-2 Type II and HIPAA); custom Enterprise (SAML SSO, on-prem). Noted around £20 for 100K requests.
tools.best_for: Teams prioritizing simple setup and granular cost tracking/optimization at the gateway layer.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B) Weave
tools.monitors: LLM application traces, experiments, model evaluations, and the end-to-end ML/LLM development lifecycle.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Integrates ML experiment tracking with LLM observability
tools.pricing: Free personal tier; usage/seat-based paid plans for teams; custom Enterprise pricing for larger deployments.
tools.best_for: ML teams already using W&B for experiment tracking who want unified LLM evaluation and observability.

tools.name: Arize AI (Phoenix)
tools.monitors: Enterprise LLM and ML telemetry, embeddings, drift, performance, and production trace data.
features: Extends long-standing ML monitoring to LLMs
tools.pricing: Arize Phoenix is free and open source (self-hosted); Arize AX enterprise platform uses custom/consumption-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Enterprises needing robust, scalable telemetry and drift monitoring across both ML and LLM workloads.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: LLM traces, prompt/response pairs, token costs, latency, and online evaluation metrics.
features: Self-hostable with a generous cloud free tier
tools.pricing: LangFuse Cloud free for under 50K requests, then usage-based (approx. £20 for 500K); Self-hosted around £30/month infra plus ~2 hours/month maintenance.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting popular, flexible open-source tracing with a low-cost or free entry point.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, vector DB queries, and framework operations via OpenTelemetry-based instrumentation, exportable to any OTel-compatible backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and frameworks
Vendor-neutral export to existing observability backends (Datadog, New Relic, Grafana, etc.)
Trace spans for prompts, completions, and tool calls
tools.pricing: Free and open source (SDK); costs depend on the chosen OTel backend. Hosted option available via Traceloop with usage-based pricing.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability stacks.

cost_tips: Implement response caching (e.g., via a gateway like Helicone) so identical or similar prompts reuse stored completions instead of triggering new paid API calls.
Route requests to the cheapest model that meets quality requirements, reserving expensive frontier models only for complex tasks and using smaller/distilled models for simple ones.
Track and optimize token usage by trimming system prompts, truncating context, summarizing long histories, and setting sensible max_token limits to avoid paying for unnecessary output.
Use observability dashboards to monitor per-feature and per-user cost, set budget alerts, and identify high-cost outliers or runaway agent loops before they inflate your bill.
